text:
maria-finance: SlateProcure trial invoice attached — numbers don't match our expected token->compute mapping. They report 12,400 compute units for March, our estimator maps that to ~3.1M tokens which would be ~$3,100 but their sample invoice shows $1,180. Anyone seen their unit definition?

alex-eng: I pulled their trial export. Their CU = 1 compute unit is measured in 'model-steps' not tokens. Rough conversion: 1 CU ≈ 256 tokens for short prompts but it varies with sequence length and response size. Pasting sample rows from the export:```usage_date,compute_units,model
2026-03-01,4200,redwood-open-13
2026-03-05,3800,redwood-open-13
2026-03-12,4200,redwood-open-70```
sasha-ops: Can we get a normalized per-1M token rate? Need that to compare to our per-token pricing and to model cost for user features.
tanvi-legal: Also flag: their T&C has auto-renew + a pricing escalator clause buried in section 5.2. We should ask for either a cap or explicit enterprise terms.
kevin-sales: Rep said they'd share a conversion table and a sample invoice mapping SKUs to CUs. @slate-rep can you drop that here? :slightly_smiling_face:
slate-rep: slate-rep: Sorry about the confusion — CU = 1 CU per 1k model-steps. Mapping is sequence-length dependent; for sanity: short seq (<=256 tokens) ~1 CU per 256 tokens, medium (257-1024) ~1 CU per 512 tokens, long (>1024) ~1 CU per 1024 tokens. We'll attach a normalized CSV and a breakdown by model. For renewal, we can offer a 7% yearly cap for enterprise customers.
maria-finance: Can you post an example invoice line showing unit price, qty (CU), and total? The sample I got doesn't include SKU mapping. Also, our procurement requires net30; their site shows net15.
billing-bot: billing-bot: invoice_2026-03-sample.pdf uploaded to thread (link: https://files.slack/slate/invoice_2026-03-sample.pdf)
alex-eng: Quick back-of-envelope: applying their midline mapping to the 12,400 CUs gives ~3.1M tokens which at our target $1 per 1k tokens would be ~$3,100 — so the $1,180 invoice looks like it used a trial discount or a different pricing tier. Need their raw billing export to reconcile.
sasha-ops: :eyes: I'll request the full billing export for the trial account from their billing team and reconcile with the telemetry export. Putting a 24h ETA on the export.
kevin-sales: If they can do net30 and a commit discount, we can convert pilot -> paid. I'll push for a 20% commit credit on first 6 months.
tanvi-legal: Don't accept auto-renew without minimum 60-day notice. Add a 30-day termination-for-convenience clause.
slate-rep: slate-rep: Confirmed: we'll provide the normalized CSV and sample invoice line by EOD. Net30 is acceptable. Commit discount requires internal approval but we'll propose 15-20%.
maria-finance: Thanks. Action items: @sasha-ops get billing export; @slate-rep send CSV + invoice example; @kevin-sales negotiate commit discount and ensure no auto-renew without notice. Reopen this thread when we have the files.
sasha-ops: Got it. Export requested, ETA ~24h.
